channel.title: NetSec Atlas — Practical Network, Security & IT Knowledge
channel.description: The latest practical articles on networking, cybersecurity and infrastructure from NetSec Atlas.

item.title: Deploying ZTNA with FortiGate and FortiClient EMS
item.description: How Fortinet ZTNA fits together: EMS certificates and posture tags, the FortiGate access proxy and policy, a first protected app, and a sane migration path off VPN.

item.title: Build a Free Home SOC Lab with Wazuh and Sysmon
item.description: Stand up Wazuh, ship Sysmon telemetry from a Windows VM, fire safe attack simulations and practise triage like a SOC analyst, all on free software.

item.title: Writing a Custom Wazuh Rule to Catch Brute-Force Logins
item.description: Build correlation rules in Wazuh that flag SSH and RDP password guessing at thresholds that fit your environment, test them with wazuh-logtest and wire them to active response.

item.title: Palo Alto NAT Explained with Worked Examples (SNAT, DNAT, U-Turn)
item.description: Worked PAN-OS NAT examples: DIPP for outbound, static and destination NAT for published servers, U-turn hairpinning, and the pre-NAT/post-NAT rule that trips everyone up.

item.title: Network Security Engineer Roadmap for 2027: What to Learn, in Order
item.description: A staged, lab-first learning plan for aspiring network security engineers: fundamentals, one firewall in depth, VPN and identity, logging, cloud and automation, plus where certifications fit.

item.title: Your First Vulnerability Scan with Nessus Essentials
item.description: Install the free Nessus Essentials scanner, run an unauthenticated and a credentialed scan on lab hosts, and turn the results into a sensible fix list.

item.title: Turning MITRE ATT&CK into Working Detections: A Practical Method
item.description: Pick the ATT&CK techniques that matter to you, map them to the logs you actually have, write and test detections, and track coverage honestly instead of colouring in a matrix.

item.title: 15 Microsoft 365 Security Settings to Check Today
item.description: Fifteen Microsoft 365 settings that shut the most common doors attackers use, grouped by identity, admin roles, email, sharing and auditing, with where to find each one.

item.title: Site-to-Site IPsec Between FortiGate and Palo Alto: Build and Troubleshoot
item.description: A route-based IKEv2 tunnel between FortiOS and PAN-OS: a shared parameter sheet, both configurations, proxy-ID pitfalls and the debug commands that find the fault.

item.title: FortiGate Initial Setup for Production: A Step-by-Step Build
item.description: Take a new FortiGate from factory defaults to production: firmware path, admin lockdown, interfaces and zones, routing, policy design, logging and backups.

item.title: Common Firewall Misconfigurations and How to Audit for Them
item.description: Ten firewall mistakes that show up in almost every audit, from any-any rules and exposed admin interfaces to missing egress filtering, plus a quarterly review routine that catches them.

item.title: A Baseline Conditional Access Policy Set for Microsoft Entra ID
item.description: The Conditional Access policies every Entra ID tenant should start with: MFA for admins and users, legacy auth blocked, Azure management covered, break-glass accounts and a safe rollout.

item.title: Why Your Company Email Goes to Spam: Diagnosing SPF, DKIM and DMARC
item.description: A methodical way to find out why your mail lands in junk: read Authentication-Results, test SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment, check reputation, and meet Gmail and Outlook sender rules.

item.title: Key Windows Security Event IDs for SOC Teams: What to Monitor and Why
item.description: Reference table of key Windows security events — logons, accounts and groups, Kerberos, processes, services, scheduled tasks, log clearing — and the audit policy they need.

item.title: KES 12 Exclusions in Kaspersky Security Center: Safe Setup and XML Import
item.description: The difference between scan exclusions and trusted applications in KES 12, how to add them in policy, import them as XML, and avoid dangerous blind spots.

item.title: Kerberoasting: How It Works, How to Detect and Prevent It
item.description: Why any domain account can attack service accounts, how to detect it with event 4769, and how to prevent it with gMSAs, long passwords and AES.

item.title: SSL VPN Tunnel Mode Removed in FortiOS 7.6.3: A Migration Plan to IPsec VPN
item.description: What changed in FortiOS 7.6.3, why you must migrate before upgrading, and how to move users, groups and policies to IPsec over TCP 443 step by step.

item.title: FortiClient Error -7200 in SSL VPN: Causes and Fixes
item.description: Error -7200 rarely means a wrong password. The real causes in order — tunnel mode after FortiOS 7.6.3, portals, cipher strength, certificates — plus debug commands.

item.title: Summer 2026 Security Roundup: SonicWall, N-central, Azure and Rails
item.description: Two actively exploited bugs (SonicWall SMA1000, N-able N-central), a huge Azure CLI password spray, and two serious flaws fixed before exploitation (Cosmos DB, Rails), with what to do about each.

item.title: Rolling Out DMARC from p=none to p=reject: A Phased Plan
item.description: A practical four-phase plan: inventory and monitoring, fixing alignment, gradual quarantine, then reject — with DNS record examples and common pitfalls.

item.title: Enterprise Email Security: The Complete Guide to SPF, DKIM and DMARC
item.description: How to protect your domain and users: SPF, DKIM and DMARC authentication, Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook sender requirements, MTA-STS, mail gateways and phishing awareness.

item.title: Endpoint Security and Vulnerability Management: The Complete Guide
item.description: Build an integrated programme: asset inventory, endpoint protection and EDR, safe exclusions, scanning, CVSS/EPSS/KEV prioritisation and patching.

item.title: Active Directory and Identity Security: The Complete Guide
item.description: Why attackers go after Active Directory first and how to protect it: the tier model, service accounts, Kerberos, LAPS, Group Policy and monitoring.

item.title: SOC and Incident Response: The Complete Guide
item.description: How to build a realistic detection and response capability: log sources, SIEM, detection rules, NIST response phases, playbooks and the metrics that matter.

item.title: Enterprise Network Security: The Complete Guide
item.description: Design a secure enterprise network: defense layers, firewall policy, remote access after SSL VPN tunnel mode removal, segmentation and monitoring.

item.title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): A Practical Guide and Methods Compared
item.description: Every type of two-factor authentication, how to set it up correctly, and the common attacks targeting it with how to protect yourself.

item.title: FortiGate SSL VPN Setup Checklist for FortiOS 7.4 and Early 7.6 (Before Tunnel Mode Goes)
item.description: The five pieces a working FortiGate SSL VPN needs on releases that still have tunnel mode, the usual reasons it fails, a hardening list, and what changes from FortiOS 7.6.3 onward.

item.title: Password Managers at Work: Why They Matter and How to Roll One Out
item.description: Why reused passwords are the real problem, how password managers work, what to look for in a business product, and a rollout plan that people will actually adopt.

item.title: Secure Remote Work: A 12-Point Control Checklist for IT Teams
item.description: Twelve controls that cover identity, devices, access, data and people for staff working from home or on the road, in priority order, with notes on how to verify each one.

item.title: The OWASP Top 10 (2025) for Busy Teams: What Each Risk Means in Practice
item.description: A plain-English tour of the OWASP Top 10:2025, from broken access control to mishandled exceptional conditions, with a worked SQL injection example and advice on using the list without treating it as a checklist.

item.title: Office Printing for IT Teams: Spooler, Drivers, Network Printers and PrintNightmare
item.description: A support-desk method for office printing problems that also closes the security gaps: spooler fixes, network printers, Point and Print after PrintNightmare, and where to disable the service.

item.title: Zero-Day Vulnerabilities: What They Are and How to Be Ready
item.description: What makes a vulnerability a zero-day, how they're found, traded and exploited, why edge devices are frequent targets, and the resilience measures that limit damage before a patch exists.

item.title: Reading CVSS Scores Properly: What the Number Hides and What to Add
item.description: How CVSS base metrics are built (attack vector, complexity, privileges, user interaction, impact), what changed in CVSS 4.0, and how to combine the score with exploitation data (KEV, EPSS) and your own exposure.

item.title: Data Loss Prevention (DLP): Covering the Channels Without Drowning in Alerts
item.description: Where data leaves an organisation (email, endpoints, cloud, web), how DLP detects sensitive content, and a phased rollout from audit to enforcement that users will tolerate.

item.title: BYOD Without Regret: Policy and Controls for Personal Devices at Work
item.description: Deciding what personal phones and laptops may access, MAM versus full MDM enrolment, the minimum security requirements, privacy boundaries, and what happens when a device is lost or an employee leaves.

item.title: Nmap for Network Admins: Core Scans, Useful Options and Staying Authorised
item.description: Practical Nmap usage for inventory and security checks: host discovery, port and service scans, OS detection, NSE scripts, output formats, timing, and the authorisation rules you must follow.

item.title: Wireshark for Troubleshooting and Security: Capture Smart, Filter Fast
item.description: Where to capture, capture versus display filters, the filters admins use most, following streams, reading TLS traffic, and real cases from slow applications to suspicious beaconing.

item.title: Threat Modeling with STRIDE: Finding Design Flaws Before You Build
item.description: A practical walkthrough of STRIDE threat modeling: drawing a data-flow diagram, applying the six threat categories, choosing mitigations, and fitting it into normal development and change work.

item.title: The TLS Handshake Step by Step: What Happens Before the Padlock Appears
item.description: How a TLS 1.3 connection is set up (Client Hello, key exchange, certificate verification, Finished), what changed from TLS 1.2, and how to troubleshoot common handshake failures.

item.title: Windows LAPS: Unique, Rotating Local Admin Passwords on Every Machine
item.description: Why one shared local admin password lets attackers hop across a whole fleet, how Windows LAPS fixes it with per-device rotated passwords stored in AD or Entra ID, and how to deploy it safely.

item.title: Web Application Firewalls: What a WAF Blocks and When It's Worth Deploying
item.description: How WAFs inspect HTTP traffic with signatures, rule sets and anomaly scoring, deployment options from cloud to on-prem, tuning without breaking the app, and why a WAF complements secure code rather than replacing it.

item.title: Securing Containers from Build to Runtime
item.description: The container security layers that matter: trusted images, least-privilege runtime settings, Kubernetes access control and network policies, secrets handling, and runtime monitoring.

item.title: Disaster Recovery Planning: Setting RTO and RPO and Proving You Can Hit Them
item.description: How to build a disaster recovery plan that works: business impact analysis, recovery time and recovery point objectives, recovery tiers, runbooks, and the testing that turns a document into a capability.

item.title: Immutable Backups: Making Sure Ransomware Can't Delete Your Way Back
item.description: Why attackers target backups first, how immutability works (object lock, WORM, hardened repositories), choosing retention, the compliance-versus-governance trade-off, and testing restores.

item.title: Authentication vs Authorization: Who You Are Versus What You May Do
item.description: A clear explanation of authentication and authorization with everyday IT examples, how protocols like Kerberos, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and SAML fit, and the common bugs when the two are confused.

item.title: How a SIEM Works: From Raw Logs to an Alert Worth Answering
item.description: What a SIEM actually does between collecting logs and paging an analyst: parsing, normalisation, correlation and tuning, with a worked example of a real detection.

item.title: How EDR Works and Why It Isn't Just Better Antivirus
item.description: What endpoint detection and response records, how it detects attacks that signature antivirus misses, the response actions it gives analysts, and what it takes to run one well.

item.title: PKI and the Chain of Trust: How a Certificate Proves Who's on the Other End
item.description: How public key infrastructure works: key pairs, certificate authorities, root and intermediate certificates, chain validation, revocation, and the operational basics of running an internal CA.

item.title: Supply Chain Attacks: Managing the Risk That Arrives Through Trusted Vendors
item.description: How attackers compromise software updates, service providers and open-source packages to reach many victims at once, and the vendor-risk and technical controls that limit the damage.

item.title: PowerShell for Sysadmins: From First Commands to Reliable Automation
item.description: The core ideas that make PowerShell different (cmdlets, objects, the pipeline), everyday commands for services, processes, files and AD, a first real script with logging and error handling, and the mistakes to avoid.
